review_basis:
A fresh, previously-untouched real project this session: a ME BGS Health Science Center project, sheet PL1.2 (page 33, plumbing) carrying three individually-scattered `3/4" CD` (condensate drain) callouts, each with its own directional note (`DN TO AC-1`, `DN TO (E) MOP SINK`), not tightly-paired mechanical-room piping. A local grid sweep of the three found one real, size-bound `trace_run` hit (25.71 LF, `pipe:0.75`, `CD`, `dead_end`/`dead_end`, zero elbows -- a perfectly straight single segment).

Confirmed via marked render crop: the traced line is a real, solid, straight horizontal condensate line with its own printed `3/4" CD` label sitting DIRECTLY centered on top of the line itself (no offset leader at all, the cleanest possible label-to-ink binding this session has seen), running between two real T-junctions -- a vertical drop on the left labeled separately (`3/4" CD DN TO AC-1`, its own diagonal leader visibly terminating on that OTHER, different vertical segment, not this one) and a vertical drop on the right at a valve/tee symbol labeled separately again (`3/4" CD DN TO (E) MOP SINK`, its own diagonal leader likewise confirmed to terminate on that different, lower vertical segment). Both of this run's own real dead ends sit exactly on the real ink; neither neighboring label's leader crosses or touches the traced horizontal segment itself, ruling out the leader-line mislabeling risk multiple other candidates were rejected for this same day.
scope: A single real 3/4" CD (condensate drain) horizontal branch line (25.71 LF, zero elbows) on the Health Science Center project's own sheet PL1.2 (page 33), between two real T-junctions (a drop from AC-1 above, a drop to an existing mop sink below), each fed by its own separately-labeled vertical segment explicitly OUT OF SCOPE for this run. Also out of scope: every other CD/plumbing callout on this same 59-sheet real project, not swept.
